scan: R = QH et S = PG (crop p133_s3_necess.png)
note: Authors' slip, kept by the TeX. e″R(t″) = 0 means R lies in the kernel G.A[T] of T ↦ t″ (B″ ≅ A[T]/G.A[T], e″G(t″) = 0), so R is a multiple of G, and S (with e′S(t′) = 0) a multiple of H; G and H are swapped. Check with F = T(T−1) over a field: e′ = 1−T = −G, e″ = T = H. Correct reading R = PG et S = QH, which keeps the printed PG+QH = 1+LF that follows (equivalently R = QG, S = PH with QG+PH = 1+LF). No erratum.
